skill.name: managing-relationships
skill.description: Manages GitHub parent and sub-issue relationships, dependency views, and tracking links through authenticated GraphQL operations.
skill.summary: Create, inspect, and verify GitHub issue relationships with GraphQL helpers.
skill.author: C0ntr0lledCha0s

security_audit.summary: The subprocess calls use fixed argument arrays without shell execution, and the Markdown detections are formatting rather than executable backticks. The skill can change authenticated GitHub relationships without an explicit confirmation requirement.

remediation.issue: Authenticated relationship mutations lack a required confirmation step.
remediation.suggestion: Require confirmation before adding, removing, or replacing relationships. Show the repository and issue numbers before execution.

content.value_statement: GitHub issue hierarchies are difficult to manage with the standard issue CLI. This skill uses GraphQL helpers to create, inspect, and verify relationships.
actual_capabilities: Adds and removes sub-issue relationships using GitHub GraphQL mutations.
Lists sub-issues and completion summaries for a selected issue.
Finds an issue parent and displays full relationship details.
Resolves GitHub node IDs from issue numbers.
Displays blocking, blocked-by, and tracking relationships.
limitations: Requires an authenticated gh CLI with suitable repository permissions.
Dependency relationships are read-only because the script does not provide dependency mutations.
Works with the current repository selected by gh.
GitHub rate limits and permissions can prevent operations.

use_cases.title: Build an issue hierarchy
use_cases.description: Connect existing epics, features, and tasks as parent and sub-issues, then verify the resulting structure.

use_cases.title: Audit repository relationships
use_cases.description: Inspect parents, children, blockers, and tracking links before reorganizing an active backlog.

use_cases.title: Review release blockers
use_cases.description: List blocking and blocked-by relationships to identify unresolved work affecting a release.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect one issue
prompt_templates.prompt: Show all relationships for issue #42 in the current repository. Do not change anything.
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with a read-only relationship check.

prompt_templates.title: Add verified sub-issues
prompt_templates.prompt: Add issues #43 and #44 under #42. Confirm the repository and planned changes before execution, then verify the result.
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a simple parent and child structure.

prompt_templates.title: Create a nested hierarchy
prompt_templates.prompt: Make #100 parent of #101 and #102, then make #101 parent of #103. Check current parents, request confirmation, apply, and verify.
prompt_templates.scenario: Build a multi-level hierarchy from existing issues.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze dependency health
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze dependencies for issues #200 through #210. Identify open blockers, hierarchy gaps, and conflicting parents. Return a prioritized plan without modifying GitHub.
prompt_templates.scenario: Perform an advanced read-only backlog audit.

best_practices: Inspect current parents and relationships before making changes.
Confirm the repository and issue numbers before every mutation.
Verify the resulting hierarchy after each operation.
anti_patterns: Do not replace an existing parent without explicit approval.
Do not treat task-list links as true sub-issue relationships.
Do not create deep hierarchies that are difficult to navigate.

faq.question: What authentication does this skill require?
faq.answer: It requires an authenticated gh CLI with permission to read issues and modify sub-issue relationships.

faq.question: Can it create new GitHub issues?
faq.answer: No. It manages relationships between existing issues.

faq.question: Can one issue have multiple parents?
faq.answer: No. GitHub allows one parent for each sub-issue.

faq.question: Can it modify blocking dependencies?
faq.answer: No. The included script only reads blocking and blocked-by relationships.

faq.question: Does it work across repositories?
faq.answer: The script operates on the current repository reported by gh.

faq.question: How does it avoid unintended changes?
faq.answer: Review the repository and issue numbers, request confirmation, and verify relationships after each mutation.
